divergence_note: This episode starts inside a physical handoff, follows a single coral mug between a mobile robot and an older participant, opens the room into research settings, then gives the participant control of the doorway. It replaces the prior exploded paperwork and vertical borehole with eye-level domestic action and a continuous human-scale relationship.

throughline.subject: The coral mug offered by the robot to the same participant
throughline.closing_state: supported within reach as a research goal, not a proven patient benefit

cinematic_contract.button: The handoff can reach the person while the research still has work ahead.

fauna_scope.reason: Indoor assistive robotics research and participant choice contain no animal-related fact.

documentary.viewer_question: Does offering a cup mean the robot has helped the person?
documentary.payoff: The visible reach gap makes task completion different from useful assistance.
documentary.source_limit: Reach adjustment is a proposed research goal; the reported photograph is a simulated apartment and the sources establish no care outcome.
documentary.hero_image: A coral mug moves from an unreachable robot grip toward the same human hand.
documentary.closing_answer: The goal is assistance within the persons reach; testing and participant choice remain work to do.

captions.text: A robot can offer a cup and still miss the person.
At UT Austin, a federally funded research center began its award term this month.
A robot could adjust its reach to a person.
The point is to bring the drink where that person can reach it.
The harder test is sharing homes and care settings over time.
The university pictures a mug handoff in a simulated apartment.
Its announcement says consent and opt out procedures will be developed.
The community is meant to help shape where and how a robot is deployed.
The useful handoff ends within reach.
The research still has to get there.

retime_evidence._why: A cut is placed at the start of the line its scene carries. That word's time is measured when the reader paused before it and modelled by syllable weight when they did not, so this counts both rather than claiming all are measured.
